clue.text: A suggestion put before the Union?

definitions.text: A suggestion put before the Union?

parts.words: A suggestion put before the Union?
parts.note: reads like a motion tabled at a debating society such as the Oxford Union, but the union meant is a marriage, and the suggestion is the offer that comes before it

explanation.surface: A motion is tabled at a student debating society.
explanation.walkthrough: The Union looks like a debating society or trade union; here it is the union of marriage, and what is put before it is the offer to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer of marriage is the classic suggestion made ahead of a wedding.

clue.text: Flyers (the whole lot) shelter in this weather

indicators.note: the flyers shelter the next word, holding it within them

parts.note: the RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force, are flyers
the whole lot means all

explanation.surface: Airmen, every one of them, take cover from the bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelter' is a container signal: the flyers hold the little word 'in', which looks like a link word but supplies letters. 'weather' is the definition, sitting after the link 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: A downpour is a kind of weather, a wet spell of it.

clue.text: Harlot from Berkshire working on a galley?

parts.note: pro is short for prostitute, a harlot
of can mean from, as in a man of Kent
Reading is the county town of Berkshire, so someone from Berkshire may be 'of Reading'

explanation.surface: A prostitute from an English county is toiling aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a large town in Berkshire, a county west of London. A galley is not a ship here but a galley proof, the first printed sheet a checker marks up.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is a printer's trial sheet, and checking one for errors is the task of correcting copy.

clue.text: Novel, as on sale at a particular time of the year

definitions.text: at a particular time of the year

indicators.note: novel means new, so the following letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A book goes on sale only at one time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book being sold; it is the anagram signal on AS ON SALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes round in one season, like Christmas goods, occurs at a fixed point of the year.

clue.text: Head of Latin made money, being highly erudite

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to have made money is to have earned

explanation.surface: A Latin teacher made a fortune and was very scholarly.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly erudite person is deeply read and full of scholarship.

clue.text: Reprimand on finding symbol of omission quietly inserted

indicators.note: the soft letter is inserted into the omission mark, placed inside it

parts.note: a caret is the proofreader's mark showing where something has been left out
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded on finding an omission mark discreetly slipped into a text.
explanation.walkthrough: A CARET is the inverted-v mark showing where text is to be added. 'on finding' just links the parts. To carpet someone is to call them in and reprimand them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be called on the carpet is to be scolded by a superior, so the verb means to rebuke.

clue.text: Cause the downfall of some gun dog trainers

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their letters, read straight through

explanation.surface: A remark about the people who train gun dogs bringing someone to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks the run gUN DOg out of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo someone is to ruin them, bring about their fall.

clue.text: Bearing gifts, do we hear?

indicators.note: asks whether we hear it, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: gifts are presents

explanation.surface: A question about someone carrying gifts, as overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like carrying, the gifts; it means a person's dignified manner, which sounds like PRESENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's poise or carriage is their bearing, an impressive personal manner.

clue.text: He tests a faulty main flowing into two rivers

indicators.note: the faulty main runs into the first river, ending up inside it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: faulty means broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tester inspects a broken water main pouring into two rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges the letters of 'main', and 'flowing into' puts the result inside the Exe, a river in south-west England; the abbreviation for river follows. 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets and marks tests, or inspects things, is an assessor.

clue.text: Cover round the swimming pool

parts.note: a lid is a cover
O is a round shape

explanation.surface: A cover is placed around the swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air public bath, as found in British towns, is an outdoor swimming venue.

clue.text: Noisy adaptation of our best prose

indicators.note: an adaptation reshapes the following words, here their letters

explanation.surface: Our finest writing has been turned into something loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adaptation of' rearranges OUR BEST PROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstreperous behaviour is unruly and loud, so noisy is a direct synonym.

clue.text: They estimate distance for shooting-gallery keepers, according to the saying

parts.note: a shooting gallery is a range for target practice
the saying 'finders keepers' says those who find something keep it

explanation.surface: Instruments that measure distance are listed for people who run shooting galleries.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is the playground rule 'finders keepers', so keepers are finders.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical instruments that measure how far off a target is are used in gunnery and photography.

clue.text: One who sponsors a regular customer

definitions.meaning: a backer who supports an artist or cause financially
someone who habitually uses a particular shop, pub or restaurant

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a financial supporter of the arts and a habitual client of a business.

clue.text: Revised notes in a Finno-Ugric tongue

indicators.note: revised notes are rewritten, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Notes have been rewritten in a language related to Finnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' rearranges NOTES IN A; 'in a' looks like part of the surface but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of the Baltic state of Estonia belongs to the Finno-Ugric family, alongside Finnish and Hungarian.

clue.text: Party leader with a tendency to be easily persuaded

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: liable means having a tendency or likelihood to do something

explanation.surface: A party leader who tends to be easily talked round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party leader' looks like a politician; it means the first letter of Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pliable bends to others' views, being readily swayed.

clue.text: Good man in Continental capital eating English food

indicators.note: the capital eats the next letter, taking it inside
the good man goes in the capital, inside it

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France on the European Continent
St, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A good man in Paris has been eating English food.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'in' puts the saint inside the capital, and 'eating' then has that whole word swallow E, which lands between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cakes and tarts made with dough are a kind of baked food.

clue.text: Unfavourable to arrange publicity without backing it

indicators.note: without means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: to advertise is to arrange publicity

indicators.note: backing means the small word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone finds it unhelpful to arrange publicity without supporting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IT into TI, and 'without' removes those letters from ADVERTISE. 'backing' looks like support.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile or harmful conditions, such as bad weather, are unfavourable.

clue.text: Reveal a girl's hiding-place

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so a girl's is Di's
cover is a place to hide, as in taking cover

explanation.surface: A young woman's secret hiding-place is exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to find out or make known what was hidden.

clue.text: Miss Cole's awful grammatical blunder

indicators.note: awful means terrible, so the name's letters are in a bad state, rearranged

parts.note: the name Miss Cole, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A woman named Miss Cole makes a terrible grammatical error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges MISS COLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a mistake in grammar or usage, a howler in speech or writing.

clue.text: Fed up with a University officer's neglect of duty

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Lt, lieutenant, is an army officer

explanation.surface: A university officer is fed up with being accused of neglecting his duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF in this down clue; 'Fed up' looks like annoyed. 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Failure to perform an obligation, especially to repay a debt, is a lapse in duty.

clue.text: Retired gentleman in a French composer's burlesque

indicators.note: the reversed title goes in the composer's name, inside it

parts.note: Erik Satie was a French composer

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A retired gentleman appears in a French composer's comic work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like describing the gentleman's career; it signals reading the title backwards. 'burlesque' looks like a noun but is a verb here, meaning to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To burlesque something is to mock it by exaggerated imitation, to lampoon it.

clue.text: Debated where to put bat? Certainly

indicators.note: asks for the spot in the clue's first word where the three letters of bat sit, so the solver gives that location as the answer

parts.note: the clue word debated is the word for an act with bat placed inside it

explanation.surface: A question about where a bat should be put, answered with emphatic agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer split as two words is the location 'where to put bat' to make DEBATED, since DEBATED is DEED with BAT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb is an emphatic affirmation, meaning truly or of course.

clue.text: It gives protection in his muddled old age

indicators.note: muddled means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: eld is an archaic word for old age

explanation.surface: His muddled mind in old age is a kind of protective cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddled' rearranges HIS; ELD is an old poetic word for old age.
explanation.definitionFit: A shield is a defensive plate a warrior carries to guard against blows.

clue.text: Unpolished type — hairy one in a suit

parts.note: rough can mean hairy or shaggy, as of a coat
diamonds are one of the four suits in a pack of cards, so a diamond is a card in that suit

explanation.surface: A coarse fellow, a hairy one in a business suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing; it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is kind-hearted but lacks manners and refinement is likened to an uncut gem.

clue.text: Strong impulse not to start a witch-hunt

indicators.note: not to start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a purge is a campaign to root out opponents, a witch-hunt

explanation.surface: A strong desire not to begin a witch-hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to start' drops the P from PURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful desire or drive to do something is a compulsion.

clue.text: Chieftain shows hesitation about military intelligence

indicators.note: about means around, so the hesitation goes around the next part

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A tribal chief hesitates when asked about military intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' is a link word. 'Chieftain' is fair: an emir is a ruler or commander in the Muslim world.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or commander, a chief in Arab lands.

clue.text: Encourage female students to collect thin porcelain

parts.note: to egg on is to encourage
she is the female pronoun
L is a learner driver, so two students are LL

explanation.surface: Female students are encouraged to collect fine china.
explanation.walkthrough: L is a learner, from the L-plate on British learner drivers' cars; two of them make LL. 'to collect' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Very fine translucent china is named for its resemblance to the delicate casing of a bird's egg.

clue.text: Unfamiliar rite not all find tedious

indicators.note: unfamiliar means changed from the usual, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: some means not all of a group

explanation.surface: Some people find an unfamiliar ritual boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfamiliar' rearranges RITE into TIRE; 'find' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome wearies and bores, being dull and annoying.
